 BTS brings purple wave to Kaohsiung as Asia tour kicks off

 Close summary BTS began the Asian and Australian leg of its ARIRANG world tour in Kaohsiung on Thursday, with performances at Kaohsiung National Stadium and citywide celebrations. Landmarks and public spaces are being illuminated in purple, while special transport and fan events add to the welcome. The regional schedule covers nine cities and 26 performances, including four Singapore concerts in December. BTS also won Most Popular International Artist at the 2026 ARIA Awards in Sydney on Wednesday.
 Key Facts
 BigHit Music said the tour includes 21 concerts across Kaohsiung, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Jakarta, Hong Kong and Bulacan before five Australian shows in Melbourne and Sydney in February.
 Kaohsiung’s BUS 613 shuttle bus references BTS’ June 13 debut anniversary, and purple hearts and ARMY-themed messages have been added to pedestrian signals, airport photo zones and subway displays.
 Selected performances in Kaohsiung on Nov. 21 and Jakarta on Dec. 29 are scheduled for live viewing in movie theaters across more than 80 countries and territories.
 BTS beat nominees including Ed Sheeran, Harry Styles, Olivia Rodrigo and Taylor Swift to win Most Popular International Artist at the 2026 ARIA Awards.
 By Lee Kyung-min Published Nov 19, 2026 10:39 am KST
 Updated Nov 19, 2026 11:10 am KST
 A promotional poster celebrating BTS winning Most Popular International Artist at the 2026 ARIA Awards in Sydney / Courtesy of BigHit Music 
 BTS is turning Kaohsiung into a citywide celebration as the global K-pop sensation begins the Asian and Australian leg of its "ARIRANG" world tour on Thursday, bringing its music beyond the stadium and into streets, landmarks and public spaces. 
 The group will perform at Kaohsiung National Stadium on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday before continuing to six other Asian cities, including Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Jakarta, Hong Kong and Bulacan, for a total of 21 concerts, according to BigHit Music.
 The tour will extend to Melbourne and Sydney in February, with five additional shows in Australia, bringing the regional schedule to nine cities and 26 performances.
 Kaohsiung has prepared an elaborate welcome, illuminating landmarks including the 85 Sky Tower, Love River, Great Harbor Bridge and Kaohsiung Music Center in purple, BTS' signature color.
 The 85 Sky Tower is also projecting messages including "THE CITY IS YOURS ARMY" and "KH LOVES ARMY" across its facade, while musical fountain performances and K-pop random dance events add to festivities.
 The city has introduced a special shuttle bus named BUS 613, referencing BTS' June 13 debut anniversary, and added purple hearts and ARMY-themed messages to pedestrian signals, airport photo zones and subway displays.
 The concert excitement will also reach movie theaters, with selected performances in Kaohsiung on Nov. 21 and Jakarta on Dec. 29 scheduled for live viewing across more than 80 countries and territories.
 In December, Singapore will host four BTS concerts at National Stadium on Dec. 17, 19, 20 and 22, alongside BTS THE CITY ARIRANG SINGAPORE, a monthlong program running from Dec. 1–31.
 The initiative will feature landmark illuminations, music and light shows at Jewel Changi Airport, and a drone performance involving approximately 1,500 drones on Sentosa Island.
 Adding to the group's momentum, BTS won Most Popular International Artist at the 2026 ARIA Awards in Sydney on Wednesday, beating nominees including Ed Sheeran, Harry Styles, Olivia Rodrigo and Taylor Swift.
